evidence: This is a sequence analysis observation, with reference to Figure 1C and a citation.

claim: The previously described anti-EPS15 Nb does not bind to the native EPS15 protein efficiently.
source: In agreement, the previously described anti-EPS15 Nb does not contain an NPF within CDR3 (Figure 1C), does not bind to the native EPS15 protein efficiently (data not shown), and was originally selected to detect (denatured) EPS15 by immunoblotting (Regan-Klapisz et al., 2005).
evidence: This is an experimental observation (data not shown).

claim: The previously described anti-EPS15 Nb was originally selected to detect (denatured) EPS15 by immunoblotting.
source: In agreement, the previously described anti-EPS15 Nb does not contain an NPF within CDR3 (Figure 1C), does not bind to the native EPS15 protein efficiently (data not shown), and was originally selected to detect (denatured) EPS15 by immunoblotting (Regan-Klapisz et al., 2005).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: A Nb E_142 (NPF→APA) replacement eliminates completely the interaction with GST-EPS15 (1-314).
source: Compared with the native VHH, a Nb E_142 (NPF→APA) replacement eliminates completely the interaction with GST-EPS15 (1-314) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from a mutagenesis and pull-down assay, with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Individual internal NPF motifs generally bind to EH domains rather weakly, with an equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) of >100 μM.
source: Because of the minimal nature of the NPF SLiM, with a single hydrophobic anchor (Phe) residue, individual internal NPF motifs generally bind to EH domains rather weakly, with an equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) of >100 μM (Yamabhai et al., 1998; de Beer et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge about NPF-EH domain binding affinity, supported by citations.

claim: Cyclized (stapled) NPF peptides bind with higher apparent affinity (~10 fold) due to stabilizing conformational rigidity.
source: Cyclized (stapled) NPF peptides bind with higher apparent affinity (~10 fold, de Beer et al., 2000) due to stabilizing conformational rigidity (Yamabhai et al., 1998), since the NPF adopts a type I β-tight turn when engaging an EH domain (de Beer et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge about NPF-EH domain binding, supported by citations.

claim: The NPF adopts a type I β-tight turn when engaging an EH domain.
source: Cyclized (stapled) NPF peptides bind with higher apparent affinity (~10 fold, de Beer et al., 2000) due to stabilizing conformational rigidity (Yamabhai et al., 1998), since the NPF adopts a type I β-tight turn when engaging an EH domain (de Beer et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge, supported by a citation.

claim: The structural constraints of the overall Nb immunoglobulin (Ig) superfamily fold and the CDR3 loop increase the apparent affinity of the Nbs for the EH domain.
source: It seems likely that the structural constraints of the overall Nb immunoglobulin (Ig) superfamily fold and the CDR3 loop similarly increase the apparent affinity of the Nbs for the EH domain, although contributions of CDR1 and CDR2 are also likely.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the binding data.

claim: Contributions of CDR1 and CDR2 to nanobody binding are also likely.
source: It seems likely that the structural constraints of the overall Nb immunoglobulin (Ig) superfamily fold and the CDR3 loop similarly increase the apparent affinity of the Nbs for the EH domain, although contributions of CDR1 and CDR2 are also likely.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the binding data.

claim: The differing relative positioning of the NPF in the CDR3 loop may be responsible for the lower apparent affinity of the Nb E_3 clone and/or more involvement of the CDR1 and -2 loops in engagement of the EH3 domain.
source: The differing relative positioning of the NPF in the CDR3 loop may be responsible for the lower apparent affinity of the Nb E_3 clone and/or more involvement of the CDR1 and -2 loops in engagement of the EH3 domain.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the binding data.

claim: The immobilized GST-EPS15 (1-314) EH1-3 array interacts physically with several NPF-harboring cytosolic partners from HeLa cell lysate, in a dose-dependent manner.
source: As a protein–protein interaction module, in biochemical pull-down assays, the immobilized GST-EPS15 (1-314) EH1-3 array interacts physically with several NPF-harboring cytosolic partners from HeLa cell lysate, in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from pull-down assays, with reference to Figures 2B and C.

claim: The apparent affinity of NPF-harboring partners for GST-EPS15 (1-314) correlates roughly with the number of NPF SLiMs.
source: The apparent affinity correlates roughly with the number of NPF SLiMs (HRB: 5; DAB2: 5; epsin 1: 3; clathrin assembly lymphoid myeloid leukemia protein (CALM): 2) and not with the presence an extreme C-terminal NPF repeat (HRB, DAB2 and epsin 1) (Yamabhai et al., 1998), with HRB being the most avid binding partner (Doria et al., 1999; Whitehead et al., 1999; Salcini et al., 1997).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pull-down assay data, supported by citations.

claim: HRB is the most avid binding partner for GST-EPS15 (1-314).
source: The apparent affinity correlates roughly with the number of NPF SLiMs (HRB: 5; DAB2: 5; epsin 1: 3; clathrin assembly lymphoid myeloid leukemia protein (CALM): 2) and not with the presence an extreme C-terminal NPF repeat (HRB, DAB2 and epsin 1) (Yamabhai et al., 1998), with HRB being the most avid binding partner (Doria et al., 1999; Whitehead et al., 1999; Salcini et al., 1997).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pull-down assay data, supported by citations.

claim: Both major isoforms of CALM contain two NPFs, one of which is near the C-terminus but not as close as occurs in either DAB2 or HRB.
source: Both major isoforms of CALM contain two NPFs, one of which is near the C-terminus but not as close as occurs in either DAB2 or HRB.
evidence: This is sequence information about CALM.

claim: Only very limited binding of cytosolic CALM to the immobilized EH domain array is evident.
source: However, only very limited binding of cytosolic CALM to the immobilized EH domain array is evident (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from pull-down assays, with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: The engagement of cytosolic NPF partners by GST-EPS15 EH1-3 is affected by highest apparent affinity Nb E_142 protein.
source: In this assay, the engagement of cytosolic NPF partners by GST-EPS15 EH1-3 is affected by highest apparent affinity Nb E_142 protein; thus the VHH clone is function blocking.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from competition assays.

claim: Nb E_142 is function blocking.
source: In this assay, the engagement of cytosolic NPF partners by GST-EPS15 EH1-3 is affected by highest apparent affinity Nb E_142 protein; thus the VHH clone is function blocking.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the competition assay data.

claim: Supplementing HeLa cell lysate with Nb E_142 at an equimolar amount relative to the GST-EPS15 (1-314) causes a substantial loss of DAB2 and epsin 1 from the bound pellet fraction and incomplete inhibition of the HRB association.
source: Supplementing HeLa cell lysate with Nb E_142 at an equimolar amount relative to the GST-EPS15 (1-314) causes a substantial loss of DAB2 and epsin 1 from the bound pellet fraction and incomplete inhibition of the HRB association.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from competition assays.

claim: A fivefold molar excess of Nb E_142 produces near complete obstruction of HRB, DAB2 and epsin 1 interactions.
source: A fivefold molar excess of Nb E_142 produces near complete obstruction of HRB, DAB2 and epsin 1 interactions, concomitant with recovery of the bound VHH domain with the GST-EPS15 fusion in the pellet fraction (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from competition assays, with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: A W57A substitution in the EPS15 EH1 domain abolishes the association of Nb E_142 with GST-EPS15 (1-109).
source: In addition, a W57A substitution in the EPS15 EH1 domain (Whitehead et al., 1999), which involves the absolutely phylogenetically conserved Trp residue in all EH domains (Confalonieri and Di Fiore, 2002; de Beer et al., 1998; de Beer et al., 2000) and disrupts the canonical NPF interaction surface between α-helices αC and αD (Figure 2E) (Rumpf et al., 2008), abolishes the association of Nb E_142 with GST-EPS15 (1-109) (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from a mutagenesis and pull-down assay, with reference to Figures 2E and 2F and citations.

claim: The W57A mutation has a comparatively modest effect on binding in the context of the larger GST-EPS15 (1-314) fusion protein.
source: Yet the same W57A mutation has a comparatively modest effect on binding in the context of the larger GST-EPS15 (1-314) fusion protein (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from a mutagenesis and pull-down assay, with reference to Figure 2F.

claim: Nb E_142 engages EH domains as an NPF-mimicking pseudoligand that contacts a conserved interaction site upon the canonical EH domain.
source: Collectively, these data clearly indicate that Nb E_142 engages EH domains as an NPF-mimicking pseudoligand that contacts a conserved interaction site upon the canonical EH domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutagenesis and competition assay data.

claim: Both Nb E_3 and E_142 cross-react with a GST-EPS15R (1-365) fusion.
source: In line with the biochemical differences noted for GST-EPS15 (1-314) engagement, both Nb E_3 and E_142 cross-react with a GST-EPS15R (1-365) fusion, while the Nb E_142 (NPF→APA) CDR3 mutant does not (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from pull-down assays, with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: The Nb E_142 (NPF→APA) CDR3 mutant does not cross-react with GST-EPS15R (1-365).
source: In line with the biochemical differences noted for GST-EPS15 (1-314) engagement, both Nb E_3 and E_142 cross-react with a GST-EPS15R (1-365) fusion, while the Nb E_142 (NPF→APA) CDR3 mutant does not (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from pull-down assays, with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: Nb E_3 binding to EPS15R is comparatively weak.
source: Nb E_3 binding to EPS15R is comparatively weak, however.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from pull-down assays.

claim: Nb E_142 is an orthosteric, function-blocking pseudoequivalent NPF ligand for the Eps15/R protein EH domains.
source: In sum, the biochemical data indicate that Nb E_142 is an orthosteric, function-blocking pseudoequivalent NPF ligand for the Eps15/R protein EH domains.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the biochemical characterization data.

claim: Nb E_142 does not interact appreciably with GST-intersectin 1 (1-312).
source: Yet in the same binding assay, Nb E_142 does not interact appreciably with GST-intersectin 1 (1-312) although the unmistakable Nb binding to both GST-EPS15 (1–109/EH1) and GST-EPS15 (1–217/EH1 + 2) is apparent (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from pull-down assays, with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Additional non-NPF side chains must contribute to the selective binding of Nb E_142 to the EPS15/R EH domains.
source: This indicates importantly that additional non-NPF side chains must contribute to the selective binding of Nb E_142 to the EPS15/R EH domains, and likely accounts for the markedly higher apparent affinity of this Nb over the native NPF ligand for EPS15/R EH domains.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lack of binding to intersectin 1.

claim: Additional non-NPF side chains likely account for the markedly higher apparent affinity of Nb E_142 over the native NPF ligand for EPS15/R EH domains.
source: This indicates importantly that additional non-NPF side chains must contribute to the selective binding of Nb E_142 to the EPS15/R EH domains, and likely accounts for the markedly higher apparent affinity of this Nb over the native NPF ligand for EPS15/R EH domains.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the binding data.

claim: It is improbable that Nb E_142 binds to other proteins with C-terminal EH domains, like EHD1.
source: Also, since none of the anti-EPS15 Nbs display acidic residues trailing the NPF in CDR3, it makes it improbable that Nb E_142 binds to other proteins with C-terminal EH domains, like EHD1 (Kieken et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an inference based on sequence analysis and knowledge of EHD1 binding requirements, supported by a citation.

claim: Using 2 μM Nb E_142 and immobilized GST-EPS15 (1–109/EH1) varied from 0.5 to 20 μM, saturation occurs at around 10 μM and half-maximal binding occurs at ~3 μM.
source: Using 2 μM Nb E_142 and immobilized GST-EPS15 (1–109/EH1) varied from 0.5 to 20 μM, saturation occurs at around 10 μM and half-maximal binding occurs at ~3 μM (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from titration assays, with reference to Figures 3C-D.

claim: With the larger GST-EPS15 (1–314/EH1-3) fusion, half-maximal binding is also seen at ~2 μM.
source: With the larger GST-EPS15 (1–314/EH1-3) fusion, half-maximal binding is also seen at ~2 μM (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from titration assays, with reference to Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The apparent KD for Nb E_142 is roughly similar for GST-EPS15 (1–109/EH1) and GST-EPS15 (1–314/EH1-3) fusion proteins.
source: That the apparent KD for Nb E_142 is roughly similar for the two fusion proteins indicates that binding to each EH domain is independent and of similar affinity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the titration assay data.

claim: Binding of Nb E_142 to each EH domain is independent and of similar affinity.
source: That the apparent KD for Nb E_142 is roughly similar for the two fusion proteins indicates that binding to each EH domain is independent and of similar affinity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the titration assay data.

claim: Nb E_142 binds to the EH domain with low micromolar affinity at physiological ionic strength.
source: Thus Nb E_142 binds to the EH domain with low micromolar affinity at physiological ionic strength; these results demonstrate that the KD of Nb E_142 for an EH domain is considerably better than a single endogenous NPF peptide (Yamabhai et al., 1998; de Beer et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the titration assay data, compared to established knowledge about NPF peptide affinity, supported by citations.

claim: The KD of Nb E_142 for an EH domain is considerably better than a single endogenous NPF peptide.
source: Thus Nb E_142 binds to the EH domain with low micromolar affinity at physiological ionic strength; these results demonstrate that the KD of Nb E_142 for an EH domain is considerably better than a single endogenous NPF peptide (Yamabhai et al., 1998; de Beer et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the titration assay data, compared to established knowledge about NPF peptide affinity, supported by citations.

claim: Nb E_142 is an immunoprecipitation-grade reagent.
source: Nb E_142 is an immunoprecipitation-grade reagent.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Purified His6-tagged Nb E_142 bound to Ni-NTA-agarose efficiently immunoprecipitates Eps15 from both K-562 erythroleukemia cell lysates and rat brain cytosol.
source: In addition to the binary interaction with recombinant GST-EPS15 (1-314) antigen (Figure 3E), purified His6-tagged Nb E_142 bound to Ni-NTA-agarose efficiently immunoprecipitates Eps15 from both K-562 erythroleukemia cell (Lozzio and Lozzio, 1975) lysates and rat brain cytosol (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoprecipitation assays, with reference to Figure 3E and a citation.

claim: Nb E_142 recognizes the native full-length Eps15 protein.
source: This Nb thus recognizes the native full-length protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Nb E_142 quantitatively precipitates EPS15R from K-562 lysate.
source: And in agreement with Nb E_142 also interacting with EPS15R (Figure 3A), there is quantitative precipitation of EPS15R from the K-562 lysate.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoprecipitation assays, with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: FCHO1, FCHO2 and AP-2 (α subunits) co-immunoprecipitate with EPS15/R immobilized through the EH domain regions by Nb E_142.
source: Analysis of co-immunoprecipitating components shows the known EPS15/R interaction partners FCHO1, FCHO2 and AP-2 (α subunits) (Figure 2B) are co-recovered with the EPS15/R immobilized through the EH domain regions by Nb E_142 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoprecipitation assays, with reference to Figures 2B and 3E.

claim: The extent of recovery of cytosolic FCHO1/2 and AP-2 mirrors the known differential affinities.
source: The extent of recovery of cytosolic FCHO1/2, which bind to the C-terminal DPF region of EPS15/R with the μ-homology domain (μHD) (Henne et al., 2010; Reider et al., 2009; Umasankar et al., 2012), and AP-2, which binds to the DPF region of EPS15/R utilizing the appendages of the α and β2 subunits (Benmerah et al., 1996; Iannolo et al., 1997), mirrors the known differential affinities (Ma et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the immunoprecipitation data, supported by citations.

claim: NPF-dependent EH domain binding partners (HRB) do not co-precipitate with Eps15/R in the presence of Nb E_142.
source: In the same assay, NPF-dependent EH domain binding partners (HRB, Figure 3E) do not co-precipitate with Eps15/R, again in line with function-blocking Nb activity.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoprecipitation assays, with reference to Figure 3E.

claim: The diffuse, rather featureless intracellular distribution of an mNeonGreen (mNG)-tagged Nb E_142 fusion is not substantially different from the control mNG protein alone.
source: Unexpectedly, when transiently transfected into HeLa cells, the diffuse, rather featureless intracellular distribution of an mNeonGreen (mNG)-tagged (Shaner et al., 2013) Nb E_142 fusion is not substantially different from the control mNG protein alone, and is clearly distinct from the punctate pattern of endogenous EPS15 staining in these cells detected with an anti-peptide antibody recognizing the extreme C-terminus (Hinrichsen et al., 2003) (Figure 4A–E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 4A-E and citations.

claim: In fewer than half the transfected cells, small concentrations of mNG-Nb E_142 that overlap some EPS15 puncta are seen.
source: In fewer than half the transfected cells, small concentrations of mNG-Nb E_142 that overlap some EPS15 puncta are seen (Figure 4B', arrowheads).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 4B'.

claim: In some mNG-Nb E_142-expressing cells an alteration in the steady-state distribution of endogenous EPS15 is evident compared with the adjacent non-transfected cells.
source: While superficially these results suggest Nb E_142 may not function effectively as a so-called chromobody (Rothbauer et al., 2006), in some mNG-Nb E_142-expressing cells an alteration in the steady-state distribution of endogenous EPS15 is evident compared with the adjacent non-transfected cells (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 4G and a citation.

claim: The intensity of the EPS15 surface puncta is diminished in mNG-Nb E_142-expressing cells relative to adjacent non-transfected cells, indicative of less EPS15 deposition at these sites.
source: The intensity of the EPS15 surface puncta is diminished relative to adjacent non-transfected cells, indicative of less EPS15 deposition at these sites, and some limited interference with EPS15 function.
evidence: This is an experimental observation and interpretation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: In adherent cell membrane cortices from inadvertently sheared-off cells, a dim mNG-Nb E_142 signal is seen to colocalize closely with endogenous EPS15.
source: Additionally, in adherent cell membrane cortices from inadvertently sheared-off cells (identified by lack of DNA staining), a dim mNG-Nb E_142 signal is seen to colocalize closely with endogenous EPS15 (Figure 4B, arrows, and Figure 4C-E).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 4B-E.

claim: In viable cells EPS15/R deposited at clathrin coat assembly sites at the plasma membrane have EH domains locally occupied in a way that makes Nb E_142 binding unfavorable.
source: As Nb E_142 is able to robustly immunoprecipitate EPS15(R) from cytosol, and because the Nbs act as pseudoligands, these transfection data suggest that in viable cells EPS15/R deposited at clathrin coat assembly sites at the plasma membrane have EH domains locally occupied in a way that makes Nb E_142 binding unfavorable.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data, combined with the immunoprecipitation data.

claim: A tandem mNG-Nb E_142 × 3 protein construct labels punctate AP-2-positive structures at very low expression levels in HeLa cells.
source: The concept of avidity-dependent, regionalized NPF occupancy of the EPS15/R EH domains gathered at incipient clathrin-coated structures is supported experimentally by the intracellular distribution and positioning of a transiently transfected triple Nb E_142 array. In HeLa cells, compared with the single Nb E_142 fusion, a larger mNG-Nb E_142 × 3 protein construct (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) now labels punctate AP-2-positive structures at very low expression levels.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The increased efficiency of EPS15/R labeling by the polyvalent mNG-Nb E_142 × 3 reporter signifies better apparent affinity for the massed EH domains at the sites of clathrin-coat assembly.
source: Given that both the ectopic mNG-Nb E_142 and the mNG-Nb E_142 × 3 proteins each contain only a single fluorescent mNG domain, the increased efficiency of EPS15/R labeling by the polyvalent reporter (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) must signify better apparent affinity for the massed EH domains at the sites of clathrin-coat assembly.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Through avidity-based phenomena, artificially but flexibly grouped NPF-harboring Nbs can compete in vivo with the deployment multiple NPF-motifs by endogenous EH domain partner proteins.
source: This indicates that through avidity-based phenomena, artificially but flexibly grouped NPF-harboring Nbs can compete in vivo with the deployment multiple NPF-motifs by endogenous EH domain partner proteins.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data.

claim: Transient overexpression of the control GFP-FYVE2 alone results in an enlarged labeled endosome compartment in HeLa SS6 cells.
source: In HeLa SS6 cells, transient overexpression of the control GFP-FYVE2 alone, which binds to the endosomal compartment phospholipid marker phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate (PtdIns3P) (Chen and De Camilli, 2005), results in an enlarged labeled endosome compartment (Figure 5B), but the subcellular distribution of EPS15 remains undisturbed at clathrin-coated structures on the cell surface.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 5B and a citation.

claim: A C-terminal Nb E_142 extension to the GFP-FYVE2 chimera produces a dramatic alteration in steady-state EPS15 positioning.
source: A C-terminal Nb E_142 extension to the GFP-FYVE2 chimera produces a dramatic alteration in steady-state EPS15 positioning; the protein now colocalizes extensively with the clustered GFP-FYVE2-Nb E_142 fusion protein on large swollen endosomes and near completely disarranges assembly of EPS15 at typical scattered puncta on the plasma membrane (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: A fundamental tenet of coat-assisted vesicle formation is the cycling of coat protomers between a membrane-attached, assembled pool and a cytosolic, reserve pool.
source: To explain the markedly altered subcellular distribution of EPS15, note that a fundamental tenet of coat-assisted vesicle formation is the cycling of coat protomers between a membrane-attached, assembled pool and a cytosolic, reserve pool.
evidence: This is established knowledge about coat protein dynamics.

claim: EPS15 is deposited from a supply in the dispersed soluble pool.
source: If EPS15 is one of the early arriving pioneers at a nascent bud, it is deposited from a supply in the dispersed soluble pool.
evidence: This is an inference based on the concept of coat protein cycling.

claim: EPS15 cycles between a membrane-assembled and a cytosolic pool.
source: The population of EPS15 in the cytosolic fraction (Figure 3) (van Delft et al., 1997a) confirms that this coat protein too cycles between a membrane-assembled and a cytosolic pool.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoprecipitation data (Figure 3) and supported by a citation.

claim: A concentrating/multivalency effect of densely tethered Nb E_142 upon a two-dimensional membrane surface markedly increases the capacity of the Nb to capture endogenous EPS15 at that site.
source: Additionally, like the tandem mNG-Nb E_142 × 3 fusion, a concentrating/multivalency effect of densely tethered Nb E_142 upon a two-dimensional membrane surface markedly increases the capacity of the Nb to capture endogenous EPS15 at that site.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data.

claim: The endosome-bound Nb E_142 can lure EPS15 from the soluble pool, titrating out the available free EPS15 such that, over time, little is available for deposition at new clathrin bud sites.
source: The endosome-bound Nb E_142 can thus lure EPS15 from the latter soluble pool, titrating out the available free EPS15 such that, over time, little is available for deposition at new clathrin bud sites.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data.

claim: Organelle-attached Nb E_142 disturbs the steady-state balance of endogenous EPS15(R) positioning within the cell.
source: Thus organelle-attached Nb E_142 disturbs the steady-state balance of endogenous EPS15(R) positioning within the cell, and therefore does function as an intrabody.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transfection and immunofluorescence data.

claim: A mitochondria-tethered Nb E_142 fusion produces near-quantitative intracellular redistribution of endogenous EPS15 in HeLa SS6 cells.
source: Very similar near-quantitative intracellular redistribution of endogenous EPS15 in HeLa SS6 cells expressing this fusion protein, but not a control (with central FKBP12-rapamycin binding (FRB) domain instead of the Nb E_142 module), is evident (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 6A and B.

claim: EPS15 puncta disappear from the basal surface in cells expressing Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP.
source: EPS15 puncta disappear from the basal surface, and in medial confocal optical sections, cells expressing the Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP do not display assembled EPS15 puncta at the cell margins, as seen in the adjacent untransfected or Akap1-FRB-iRFP transfected cells (Figure 6B', arrows).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 6B'.

claim: Unlike GFP-FYVE2-Nb E_142 expression, even in high level expression cells, the mitochondria relocalized EPS15 does not elicit prominent AP-2 reorganization.
source: But unlike GFP-FYVE2-Nb E_142 expression, even in high level expression cells, the mitochondria relocalized EPS15 does not elicit prominent AP-2 reorganization, possibly reflecting the absence of a suitable source of phosphatidylinositol 4, 5-bisphosphate (PtdIns(4,5)P2) support on the mitochondrial outer membrane and/or the lack of suitable cargo with appropriate sorting signals to bind to the AP-2 adaptor core (Jackson et al., 2010; Traub and Bonifacino, 2013) (Figure 6C–D').
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 6C-D' and citations.

claim: Both Akap1-FRB-iRFP and Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-producing HeLa cells internalize transferrin despite the conspicuous difference in EPS15 positioning within the Nb E_142-expressing cells.
source: Functional studies show that both Akap1-FRB-iRFP and Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-producing HeLa cells internalize transferrin despite the conspicuous difference in EPS15 positioning within the Nb E_142-expressing cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B'), as is seen with the GFP-FYVE2-Nb E_142-producing cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays, with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B' and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: A small subpopulation of Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells display strongly suppressed, but not halted, transferrin internalization.
source: A small subpopulation of Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells display strongly suppressed, but not halted, transferrin internalization.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays.

claim: The diminished transferrin uptake in a fraction of cells is not likely due to mitochondrial dysfunction and ATP restriction but more probably due to the known cell-cycle dependence of transferrin endocytosis and/or heterogeneity in relative internalization dependent upon local context and positioning of the cultured cells within the adherent population.
source: Since a similar fraction (~15%) of the Akap1-FRB-iRFP fusion produces a similar phenotype, the diminished transferrin uptake is not likely due to mitochondrial dysfunction and ATP restriction but more probably due to the known cell-cycle dependence of transferrin endocytosis (Sager et al., 1984) and/or heterogeneity in relative internalization dependent upon local context and positioning of the cultured cells within the adherent population (Snijder et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transferrin uptake assay data, supported by citations.

claim: In the presence of a normal complement of endocytic clathrin coat components, artificial spatial displacement of EPS15/R onto mitochondria does not severely disrupt short-term clathrin-mediated endocytosis in parental HeLa SS6 cells.
source: Overall, in the presence of a normal complement of endocytic clathrin coat components, artificial spatial displacement of EPS15/R onto mitochondria does not severely disrupt short-term clathrin-mediated endocytosis in parental HeLa SS6 cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transferrin uptake assay data.

claim: Eps15/R and Fcho1/2 function along the same pathway in a redundant manner.
source: As Eps15/R and Fcho1/2 function along the same pathway in a redundant manner (Ma et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2016b), the effect of forced expression of the mitochondria-targeted Nb E_142 was explored in novel HeLa cells rendered FCHO1/2- and EPS15R-null by successive TALEN-mediated gene editing (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited references, used to motivate the experimental approach, with reference to Figure 7A.

claim: Three new triple-null lines were obtained that exhibit indels within the targeted exon 5 region of the EPS15R-encoding EPS15L1 gene on chromosome 19.
source: Of the three new triple-null lines obtained that exhibit indels within the targeted exon 5 region of the EPS15R-encoding EPS15L1 gene on chromosome 19 (Figure 7B), and have no detectable EPS15R protein on immunoblots (Figure 7C), one, clone #40, was selected for further analysis.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from TALEN-mediated gene editing, with reference to Figures 7B and 7C.

claim: The three new triple-null lines have no detectable EPS15R protein on immunoblots.
source: Of the three new triple-null lines obtained that exhibit indels within the targeted exon 5 region of the EPS15R-encoding EPS15L1 gene on chromosome 19 (Figure 7B), and have no detectable EPS15R protein on immunoblots (Figure 7C), one, clone #40, was selected for further analysis.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoblotting, with reference to Figure 7C.

claim: The relative cellular abundance of EPS15, AP-2 and several other clathrin-mediated endocytosis components is not changed in the HeLa clone #40 cells.
source: The relative cellular abundance of EPS15, AP-2 and several other clathrin-mediated endocytosis components is not changed in the HeLa clone #40 cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunoblotting, with reference to Figure 7C.

claim: Clone #40 cells display morphologically abnormal clathrin-coated structures at steady state.
source: Like the HeLa clone #64/1.E cells from which they are derived, clone #40 cells display morphologically abnormal clathrin-coated structures at steady state (Figure 7D–F); compared with the parental HeLa SS6 cells, fewer, larger and more clustered AP-2- and EPS15-positive clathrin assemblies are present on the ventral membrane in clone #40 cells.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunofluorescence microscopy, with reference to Figures 7D-F.

claim: Compared with the parental HeLa SS6 cells, fewer, larger and more clustered AP-2- and EPS15-positive clathrin assemblies are present on the ventral membrane in clone #40 cells.
source: Like the HeLa clone #64/1.E cells from which they are derived, clone #40 cells display morphologically abnormal clathrin-coated structures at steady state (Figure 7D–F); compared with the parental HeLa SS6 cells, fewer, larger and more clustered AP-2- and EPS15-positive clathrin assemblies are present on the ventral membrane in clone #40 cells.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from immunofluorescence microscopy.

claim: The abnormal distribution and morphology of clathrin-coated structures in the genome-edited cells implies FCHO1/2 and EPS15R play some significant role in bud site selection and maintenance.
source: This abnormal distribution and morphology of clathrin-coated structures in the genome-edited cells implies FCHO1/2 and EPS15R play some significant role in bud site selection and maintenance.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the immunofluorescence microscopy data.

claim: Both the HeLa #64/1.E and the clone #40 cells display defective clathrin-mediated endocytosis compared with parental HeLa SS6 cells.
source: Side-by-side comparison of transferrin uptake and the steady-state abundance of transferrin receptors at the cell surface reveals that both the HeLa #64/1.E (Umasankar et al., 2014) and the clone #40 cells display defective clathrin-mediated endocytosis compared with parental HeLa SS6 cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays, with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and a citation.

claim: Fluorescent transferrin is internalized into peripheral early endosomes (LAMP1-negative) in a 5 min pulse of the genome-edited cells at 37°C.
source: Although fluorescent transferrin is internalized into peripheral early endosomes (lysosome-associated membrane glycoprotein 1 (LAMP1)-negative) in a 5 min pulse of the genome-edited cells at 37°C (accounting for their long-term viability), the extent is less than in the HeLa SS6 cells.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays.

claim: The extent of transferrin internalization in genome-edited cells is less than in the HeLa SS6 cells.
source: Although fluorescent transferrin is internalized into peripheral early endosomes (lysosome-associated membrane glycoprotein 1 (LAMP1)-negative) in a 5 min pulse of the genome-edited cells at 37°C (accounting for their long-term viability), the extent is less than in the HeLa SS6 cells.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays.

claim: The majority of the transferrin is bound to transferrin receptors diffusely situated over the plasma membrane in genome-edited cells.
source: Instead, the majority of the transferrin is bound to transferrin receptors diffusely situated over the plasma membrane (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B' and C').
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays, with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1B' and C'.

claim: The data indicate slowed egress of the transferrin receptor from the surface of the genome-edited cells for reentry into the endosomal compartment, leading to stalling and accumulation of this (and other) endocytic cargo at the plasma membrane.
source: Comparative accumulation of surface transferrin receptors in the genome-edited lines is confirmed by fluorescent transferrin labeling experiments conducted on ice for 60 min (unpublished); the data thus indicate slowed egress of the transferrin receptor from the surface of the genome-edited cells for reentry into the endosomal compartment, leading to stalling and accumulation of this (and other) endocytic cargo at the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transferrin uptake assay data.

claim: Transient expression of negative control Akap1-FRB-iRFP in the HeLa clone #40 cells has no obvious effect on the subcellular patterning of EPS15.
source: Transient expression of negative control Akap1-FRB-iRFP in the HeLa clone #40 cells has no obvious effect on the subcellular patterning of EPS15 (Figure 8A), as in parental the HeLa SS6 cells.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 8A.

claim: In Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP producing clone #40 cells, ectopic trapping of EPS15 on the mitochondria-massed Nb E_142 is clear, with a concomitant loss of EPS15 from the plasma membrane.
source: By contrast, in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP producing clone #40 cells, ectopic trapping of EPS15 on the mitochondria-massed Nb E_142 is clear, with a concomitant loss of EPS15 from the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: In transfected clone #40 cells, AP-2 clusters at the surface are diminished in size and number in a manner that correlates with the efficiency of EPS15 segregation at mitochondria.
source: In these transfected clone #40 cells, AP-2 clusters at the surface are diminished in size and number in a manner that correlates with the efficiency of EPS15 segregation at mitochondria (Figure 8B-F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 8B-F.

claim: The majority of AP-2-positive puncta that do remain are populated with detectable endogenous EPS15 protein.
source: The majority of AP-2-positive puncta that do remain are populated with detectable endogenous EPS15 protein (Figure 8C–F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 8C-F.

claim: In the genetic background of clone #40 cells, stable membrane-associated AP-2 assemblies depend heavily on EPS15 for their generation.
source: Thus, in this genetic background stable membrane-associated AP-2 assemblies depend heavily on EPS15 for their generation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transfection and immunofluorescence data in clone #40 cells.

claim: Based on the apparent affinity and computed cellular abundance in HeLa cells, HRB, HRB-like protein (HRBL) and DAB2 are most likely the predominant interaction partners for the EH domains at assembling clathrin-coated structures.
source: Based on the apparent affinity and computed cellular abundance in HeLa cells (Hein et al., 2015; Itzhak et al., 2016), HRB, HRB-like protein (HRBL) and DAB2 are most likely the predominant interaction partners for the EH domains at assembling clathrin-coated structures (Figure 2).
evidence: This is an inference based on affinity data and cellular abundance data from cited references, with reference to Figure 2.

claim: In untransfected clone #40 cells, both EPS15 and HRB overlap at the aberrant enlarged clathrin-coated structures.
source: Comparison of the steady-state distribution of EPS15 and HRB in clone #40 cells shows that whereas both proteins overlap at the aberrant enlarged clathrin-coated structures that are a distinctive feature of untransfected cells, in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells, neither protein is efficiently deposited on the plasma membrane (Figure 8G–L).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 8G-L.

claim: In Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing clone #40 cells, neither EPS15 nor HRB is efficiently deposited on the plasma membrane.
source: Comparison of the steady-state distribution of EPS15 and HRB in clone #40 cells shows that whereas both proteins overlap at the aberrant enlarged clathrin-coated structures that are a distinctive feature of untransfected cells, in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells, neither protein is efficiently deposited on the plasma membrane (Figure 8G–L).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 8G-L.

claim: In Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing clone #40 cells, EPS15 is lured onto the cytosolic face of mitochondria but HRB is not.
source: In these cells, EPS15 is lured onto the cytosolic face of mitochondria but HRB is not, and EPS15 is associated with the few HRB puncta that are evident at the plasma membrane (Figure 8I–L).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 8I-L.

claim: In the presence of Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP, HRB is essentially displaced into the soluble cytosolic compartment.
source: Thus, in the presence of Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP, HRB is essentially displaced into the soluble cytosolic compartment.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data.

claim: These findings recapitulate the effect of combined EPS15 and EPS15R RNAi in the parental HeLa clone #64/1.E cells, where there is a shift from large irregular clathrin-coated assemblies to small, abortive diffraction-limited structures.
source: Overall, these findings recapitulate the effect of combined EPS15 and EPS15R RNAi in the parental HeLa clone #64/1.E cells, where there is a shift from large irregular clathrin-coated assemblies to small, abortive diffraction-limited structures (Ma et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings to previous results, supported by a citation.

claim: The defects in AP-2-containing clathrin-coated structures in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-transfected clone #40 cells translate into clathrin-mediated endocytosis dysfunction.
source: The defects in AP-2-containing clathrin-coated structures in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-transfected clone #40 cells translate into clathrin-mediated endocytosis dysfunction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transferrin uptake assay data.

claim: Loss of EPS15 from surface puncta in clone #40 cells by massing upon mitochondria with Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP has a strong inhibitory effect on transferrin uptake.
source: Loss of EPS15 from surface puncta in clone #40 cells by massing upon mitochondria with Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP has a strong inhibitory effect on transferrin uptake (Figure 9).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays, with reference to Figure 9.

claim: The presence of small intracellular endosomes positive for the fluorescent endocytic tracer is strongly decreased in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing clone #40 cells compared with the neighboring untransfected cells.
source: In both basal and medial confocal optical sections and maximal intensity projections, the presence of small intracellular endosomes positive for the fluorescent endocytic tracer is strongly decreased compared with the neighboring untransfected cells, and also with control Akap1-FRB-iRFP producing clone #40 HeLa cells (Figure 9).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transferrin uptake assays, with reference to Figure 9.

claim: The number of >0.2 μm2 transferrin-positive intracellular structures within the three-dimensional volume of untransfected cells surrounding the Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells is roughly double that of the EPS15-sequested cell population.
source: In these experiments, quantitation shows that the number of >0.2 μm2 transferrin-positive intracellular structures within the three-dimensional volume of untransfected cells surrounding the Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells is roughly double that of the EPS15-sequested cell population (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the transferrin uptake assay data, with reference to Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: The inhibited internalization with mitochondria-appropriated EPS15 implies that FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R facilitate AP-2-dependent clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
source: Since the larger transferrin-containing vesicular structures represent progressive concentrating endosomal fusion reactions (Rink et al., 2005), and because the Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-transfected HeLa clone #40 cells display substantially elevated levels of transferrin receptors at the cell surface (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), this inhibited internalization with mitochondria-appropriated EPS15 implies that FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R facilitate AP-2-dependent clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transferrin uptake assay data, with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and a citation.

claim: Ectopic expression of Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP is unlikely to grossly perturb PtdIns(4,5)P2 levels.
source: Ectopic expression of Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP is unlikely to grossly perturb PtdIns(4,5)P2 levels on the basis of the proper plasma membrane deposition of endogenous AP-2 in transfected HeLa SS6 cells (Figure 6).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of AP-2 localization in transfected cells, with reference to Figure 6.

claim: The failure of AP-2 to assemble into normally dispersed puncta at the surface of clone #40 cells is not due to bulk effects on phosphoinositide metabolism in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-transfected cells.
source: Indeed, the failure of AP-2 to assemble into normally dispersed puncta at the surface of clone #40 cells is not due to bulk effects on phosphoinositide metabolism in Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-transfected cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the PtdIns(4,5)P2 biosensor experiments.

claim: Both co-transfected Akap1-FRB-iRFP or Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells show an abundance of PtdIns(4,5)P2 at the plasma membrane even with the marked difference in EPS15 localization.
source: Using the phospholipase Cδ1 pleckstrin-homology (PH) domain as an intracellular biosensor for PtdIns(4,5)P2, both co-transfected Akap1-FRB-iRFP or Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-expressing cells show an abundance of this plasma membrane localized lipid even with the marked difference in EPS15 localization (Figure 10A and B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments using a PtdIns(4,5)P2 biosensor, with reference to Figures 10A and B.

claim: Despite a plasma membrane supply of PtdIns(4,5)P2, elevated levels of the transferrin receptor at the cell surface, and a normal cellular concentration of AP-2, the absence of utilizable FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R pioneers in HeLa clone #40 cells is not compatible with widespread and stable deposition of AP-2 at the cell surface and assembly of clathrin-coated structures.
source: These results reveal that despite a plasma membrane supply of PtdIns(4,5)P2, elevated levels of the transferrin receptor at the cell surface (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and a normal cellular concentration of AP-2 (Figure 7C), the absence of utilizable FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R pioneers in HeLa clone #40 cells is not compatible with widespread and stable deposition of AP-2 at the cell surface and assembly of clathrin-coated structures.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined data, with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Figure 7C.

claim: The noted parallel decrease in AP-2 and HRB puncta in the presence of the Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP trap supports the notion that the EH domains of EPS15/R play a key role in docking HRB at nascent coated buds.
source: In addition, the noted parallel decrease in AP-2 and HRB puncta in the presence of the Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP trap again supports the notion that the EH domains of EPS15/R play a key role in docking HRB at nascent coated buds.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transfection and immunofluorescence data.

claim: Ectopic GFP-FCHO1 (1–609) can reconstitute the regularly dispersed HeLa clathrin-coated structure pattern at very low levels of expression of the linker.
source: Fully concordant with the widely dispersed PtdIns(4,5)P2 within the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane in both Akap1-FRB-iRFP- and Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP-transfected HeLa clone #40 cells is the restoration of extensive and apparently random deposition of AP-2 on co-transfection with GFP-tagged FCHO1 (1–609) (Figure 11). This truncated FCHO1 protein contains the membrane-binding N-terminal EFC/F-BAR domain (Umasankar et al., 2012; Henne et al., 2007) and the adjoining intrinsically disordered linker that appears to operate as an allosteric activator (Umasankar et al., 2014; Hollopeter et al., 2014), driving a reconfiguration of AP-2 from the closed to the membrane-bound open state (Jackson et al., 2010). Ectopic GFP-FCHO1 (1–609) can reconstitute the regularly dispersed HeLa clathrin-coated structure pattern at very low levels of expression of the linker (Figure 11A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 11A and citations.

claim: Measurement of AP-2-positive puncta in FCHO1 linker-expressing cells, compared with adjacent non-transfected HeLa clone #40 cells, documents the overall shift to smaller, more numerous 0.2–0.6 μm2 structures.
source: Measurement of AP-2-positive puncta in FCHO1 linker-expressing cells, compared with adjacent non-transfected HeLa clone #40 cells, documents the overall shift to smaller, more numerous 0.2–0.6 μm2 structures (Figure 11—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the transfection and immunofluorescence data, with reference to Figure 11—figure supplement 1.

claim: EPS15 is sequestered prominently by the overexpressed Nb decoy on mitochondria, and little endogenous EPS15 is deposited along with the corrected AP-2 in the compact, scattered surface puncta.
source: In parallel technical replicates, as expected EPS15 is sequestered prominently by the overexpressed Nb decoy on mitochondria, and little endogenous EPS15 is deposited along with the corrected AP-2 in the compact, scattered surface puncta (Figure 11B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figure 11B.

claim: The normalizing effect of the FCHO1 (EFC domain and) linker is manifest largely in the absence of co-assembled EPS15.
source: Thus the normalizing effect of the FCHO1 (EFC domain and) linker is manifest largely in the absence of co-assembled EPS15.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transfection and immunofluorescence data.

claim: The expressed GFP-FCHO1 (1–609) produces a profusion of small clathrin-coated structures spread over the basal plasma membrane that contain both AP-2 and EPS15.
source: Also in the same experiment, by itself the expressed GFP-FCHO1 (1–609) produces a profusion of small clathrin-coated structures spread over the basal plasma membrane that contain both AP-2 and EPS15, while the transfected Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP alone repeatedly diminishes the intensity and abundance of AP-2 structures at the ventral surface of clone #40 cells (Figure 11C–D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 11C-D.

claim: The transfected Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP alone repeatedly diminishes the intensity and abundance of AP-2 structures at the ventral surface of clone #40 cells.
source: Also in the same experiment, by itself the expressed GFP-FCHO1 (1–609) produces a profusion of small clathrin-coated structures spread over the basal plasma membrane that contain both AP-2 and EPS15, while the transfected Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP alone repeatedly diminishes the intensity and abundance of AP-2 structures at the ventral surface of clone #40 cells (Figure 11C–D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 11C-D.

claim: The FCHO1-corrected phenotype is starkly different from the untransfected clone #40 cells, and closely mirrors the results seen in clone #64/1.E cells.
source: The FCHO1-corrected phenotype is starkly different from the untransfected clone #40 cells, and closely mirrors the results seen in clone #64/1.E cells (Umasankar et al., 2014; Sager et al., 1984), where we have shown this is not due to the phospholipid-binding N-terminal EFC domain (Umasankar et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings to previous results, supported by citations.

claim: These striking results verify that FCHO1/2 act epistatically to EPS15/R.
source: These striking results again verify that FCHO1/2 act epistatically to EPS15/R and demonstrate clearly that a major role of EPS15/R is normally to cooperate with full-length FCHO1/2 to bind to and activate AP-2 proteins at incipient clathrin-coated structures, as we previously suggested (Ma et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transfection and immunofluorescence data, supported by a citation.

claim: A major role of EPS15/R is normally to cooperate with full-length FCHO1/2 to bind to and activate AP-2 proteins at incipient clathrin-coated structures.
source: These striking results again verify that FCHO1/2 act epistatically to EPS15/R and demonstrate clearly that a major role of EPS15/R is normally to cooperate with full-length FCHO1/2 to bind to and activate AP-2 proteins at incipient clathrin-coated structures, as we previously suggested (Ma et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transfection and immunofluorescence data, supported by a citation.

claim: The G-Nb E_142-E3 plasmid is highly effective in promoting the degradation of EPS15 in transiently transfected cells positive for GFP.
source: The negative control, parental GFE3 transfection into HeLa SS6 cells, has negligible impact on the steady-state distribution of EPS15 at clathrin-coated puncta on the ventral cell surface (Figure 12A). By contrast, the G-Nb E_142-E3 plasmid is highly effective in promoting the degradation of EPS15 in transiently transfected cells positive for GFP (Figure 12B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 12A and 12B.

claim: Effective elimination of EPS15/R by the tailored G-Nb E_142-E3 fusion protein still leaves AP-2 assembled at clathrin-coated sites on the plasma membrane of the HeLa SS6 cells.
source: As with Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP, effective elimination of EPS15/R by the tailored G-Nb E_142-E3 fusion protein still leaves AP-2 assembled at clathrin-coated sites on the plasma membrane of the HeLa SS6 cells (Figure 12C–D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from transfection and immunofluorescence experiments, with reference to Figures 12C-D.

claim: In depth characterization of the anti-EPS15 Nb E_142 shows this VHH is a versatile reagent in that it functions both in in vitro biochemical assays and as an effective intrabody in the reducing environment of the cell cytosol.
source: In depth characterization of the anti-EPS15 Nb E_142 shows this VHH is a versatile reagent in that it functions both in in vitro biochemical assays and as an effective intrabody in the reducing environment of the cell cytosol.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the combined biochemical and cell-based data.

claim: Using new NPF motif-harboring llama Nbs, it is demonstrated that during assembly the collective EH domains of EPS15 and EPS15R deposited at clathrin-coated structures appear poorly accessible.
source: Here, using new NPF motif-harboring llama Nbs, it is demonstrated that during assembly the collective EH domains of EPS15 and EPS15R deposited at clathrin-coated structures appear poorly accessible; this provides an important clue to the occupancy of EH domains during lattice assembly and sorting in light of the known modest KD for a single NPF•EH domain interaction (Yamabhai et al., 1998; de Beer et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the cell-based data, supported by citations.

claim: These results confirm and extend previous data showing that ectopic expression of the tandem EH domain module can inhibit clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
source: These results confirm and extend previous data showing that ectopic expression of the tandem EH domain module can inhibit clathrin-mediated endocytosis (Carbone et al., 1997), and that removal of EH2 + EH3 from EPS15 prevents proper targeting to and stationing at clathrin-coated structures (Benmerah et al., 1999).
evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings to previous results, supported by citations.

claim: Inactivating point mutations to each of the three EH domains of the full-length Drosophila Eps15 orthologue abolish proper positioning at the synapse.
source: Inactivating point mutations to each of the three EH domains of the full-length Drosophila Eps15 orthologue abolish proper positioning at the synapse, while a C-terminally truncated ΔDPF mutant still localizes properly and is able to effectively rescue the defective synaptic vesicle endocytosis at eps15-null nerve terminals (Koh et al., 2007).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: A C-terminally truncated ΔDPF mutant of Drosophila Eps15 still localizes properly and is able to effectively rescue the defective synaptic vesicle endocytosis at eps15-null nerve terminals.
source: Inactivating point mutations to each of the three EH domains of the full-length Drosophila Eps15 orthologue abolish proper positioning at the synapse, while a C-terminally truncated ΔDPF mutant still localizes properly and is able to effectively rescue the defective synaptic vesicle endocytosis at eps15-null nerve terminals (Koh et al., 2007).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: In the squid giant axon, microinjection of an NPF peptide interferes with clathrin-mediated endocytosis at an early stage, roughly halving the occurrence of clathrin-coated structures at the synapse.
source: And in the squid giant axon, microinjection of an NPF peptide interferes with clathrin-mediated endocytosis at an early stage, roughly halving the occurrence of clathrin-coated structures at the synapse (Morgan et al., 2003).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: Eps15b, an alternatively-spliced isoform of Eps15 in vertebrates, lacks the N-terminal EH1-3 tandem array entirely and does not localize to the plasma membrane but rather to endosomes.
source: Eps15b, an alternatively-spliced isoform of Eps15 in vertebrates, lacks the N-terminal EH1-3 tandem array entirely and does not localize to the plasma membrane but rather to endosomes (Roxrud et al., 2008).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: The EH domain module, alone, is not able to concentrate at clathrin-coated structures.
source: Yet the EH domain module, alone, is not able to concentrate at clathrin-coated structures (Benmerah et al., 2000).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: In the budding yeast S. cerevisiae, Hs EPS15 can substitute for the orthologous Ede1p.
source: In the budding yeast S. cerevisiae, where Hs EPS15 can substitute for the orthologous Ede1p, the minimal region of Ede1p necessary for proper targeting to clathrin-coated buds is EH3, a flanking proline-rich region and the coiled-coil domain (Lu and Drubin, 2017).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: The minimal region of Ede1p necessary for proper targeting to clathrin-coated buds is EH3, a flanking proline-rich region and the coiled-coil domain.
source: In the budding yeast S. cerevisiae, where Hs EPS15 can substitute for the orthologous Ede1p, the minimal region of Ede1p necessary for proper targeting to clathrin-coated buds is EH3, a flanking proline-rich region and the coiled-coil domain (Lu and Drubin, 2017).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: EH domains play a critical role in placing Eps15 at the membrane bud site but highlights the cooperativity of the binding information hardwired into Eps15/R and their early-arriving binding partners.
source: This argues that EH domains play a critical role in placing Eps15 at the membrane bud site but highlights the cooperativity of the binding information hardwired into Eps15/R (Figure 2B) and their early-arriving binding partners.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data, with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: In metazoa, early-arriving binding partners of Eps15/R include AP-2, Fcho1/2, Hrb, Dab2, epsin, and CALM.
source: In metazoa, these include AP-2, Fcho1/2, Hrb, Dab2, epsin, and CALM (Manna et al., 2015).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: These endocytic proteins display a densely wired interactome.
source: These endocytic proteins display a densely wired interactome, and it seems likely they are responsible for high frequency occupancy of the EH domains at clathrin assembly sites.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known interactions of these proteins.

claim: Like EPS15/R, HRB/L and DAB2 are both detected in proximity labeling mass spectrometry experiments as early, and thus edge positioned, components.
source: Like EPS15/R, HRB/L (also designated AGFG1/2) and DAB2 are both detected in proximity labeling mass spectrometry experiments as early, and thus edge positioned, components (Paek et al., 2017).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: The poor labeling of clathrin-coated structures with mNG-Nb E_142 indicates not only that the EH domain module is locally occupied at these assembly zones, but that any monomeric Nb E_142 bound to incoming EPS15/R is promptly displaced by the forming EH network that accompanies coat formation.
source: Because Nb E_142 can bind efficiently to EPS15/R in the soluble state, the poor labeling at clathrin-coated structures with mNG-Nb E_142 and other tagged versions indicates not only that the EH domain module is locally occupied at these assembly zones, but that any monomeric Nb E_142 bound to incoming EPS15/R is promptly displaced by the forming EH network that accompanies coat formation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cell-based data.

claim: An increase in effective membrane concentration of the endogenous EH binding partners at nascent clathrin bud sites by two-dimensional partitioning and avidity effects slowing unbinding and diffusion away is a plausible explanation for the apparent discrepancy in Nb E_142 binding in vitro versus in vivo.
source: A plausible explanation for this apparent discrepancy is an increase in effective membrane concentration of the endogenous EH binding partners at nascent clathrin bud sites by two-dimensional partitioning and avidity effects slowing unbinding and diffusion away (Yogurtcu and Johnson, 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data, supported by a citation.

claim: The results from the new triple-null clone #40 HeLa cells expressing a mitochondria-bound Nb E_142 illustrate that without FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R, coated assemblies do not form stably and clathrin-mediated endocytosis falters.
source: The results from the new triple-null clone #40 HeLa cells expressing a mitochondria-bound Nb E_142 illustrate that without FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R, coated assemblies do not form stably and clathrin-mediated endocytosis falters.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the data in clone #40 cells.

claim: The steady-state perdurance of clathrin-coated structures depends on presence of the pioneer EPS15 in clone #40 cells, albeit with abnormal morphology.
source: Thus the steady-state perdurance of clathrin-coated structures depends on presence of the pioneer EPS15 in clone #40 cells, albeit with abnormal morphology.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in clone #40 cells.

claim: In parental HeLa cells, loss of either FCHO1/2 or EPS15/R alone does not abolish uptake.
source: However, in parental HeLa cells, loss of either set alone does not similarly abolish uptake (Ma et al., 2016; Umasankar et al., 2012; Teckchandani et al., 2012) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is information from cited references and data from the current study, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: To explain the compensation between FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R, there must be a shared partner protein(s) that is bound to both these pioneers, and can still operate in the absence of one.
source: To explain this compensation, there must be a shared partner protein(s) that is bound to both these pioneers, and can still operate in the absence of one.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed compensation.

claim: Potential candidates for a critical common partner are AP-2 and/or its direct binding partners DAB2, CALM, HRB or epsin.
source: Again, this is emblematic of the extensive redundancy in the pioneer interaction web (Figure 2B). Potential candidates for a critical common partner are once more AP-2 and/or its direct binding partners DAB2, CALM, HRB or epsin.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the data, with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Both CALM and HRB operate as vital SNARE retrieving sorting adaptors.
source: Both CALM and HRB operate as vital SNARE retrieving sorting adaptors (Miller et al., 2011; Pryor et al., 2008).
evidence: This is information from cited references.

claim: The Nb-directed mislocalization of EPS15 in the HeLa clone #40 cells leads to bulk loss of clathrin-coated structures and diminished clathrin-based uptake.
source: That the Nb-directed mislocalization of EPS15 in the HeLa clone #40 cells leads to bulk loss of clathrin-coated structures and diminished clathrin-based uptake indicates that the EH domain proteins intersectin 1 and intersectin 2, which are both expressed in HeLa cells (Figure 4) (Itzhak et al., 2016), cannot sustain the process without FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in clone #40 cells, with reference to Figure 4 and a citation.

claim: The EH domain proteins intersectin 1 and intersectin 2 cannot sustain clathrin-mediated endocytosis without FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R.
source: That the Nb-directed mislocalization of EPS15 in the HeLa clone #40 cells leads to bulk loss of clathrin-coated structures and diminished clathrin-based uptake indicates that the EH domain proteins intersectin 1 and intersectin 2, which are both expressed in HeLa cells (Figure 4) (Itzhak et al., 2016), cannot sustain the process without FCHO1/2 and EPS15/R.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in clone #40 cells.

claim: These findings differ from siRNA-based experiments unless Nb E_142 also quantitatively depletes intersectins.
source: These findings differ from siRNA-based experiments (Teckchandani et al., 2012) unless Nb E_142 also quantitatively depletes intersectins.
evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings to previous results, supported by a citation.

claim: Nb E_142 does not bind physically to the intersectin 1 EH domains.
source: Nb E_142 does not bind physically to the intersectin 1 EH domains, and although hierarchical clustering, based on ultrastructural localization within clathrin-coated structures, places EPS15/R and intersectin in distinct branches (Sochacki et al., 2017), and the BioPlex 2.0 database (with HEK 293 cells) (Schweppe et al., 2018) does not score EPS15/R as intersectin 1 or -2 binding partners, the noted discrepancy could be due to intersectins binding physically to EPS15/R (Sengar et al., 1999) and so being concomitantly unavailable when massed at an inappropriate intracellular organelle, or due to lower cellular abundance.
evidence: This is an experimental observation and interpretation, supported by citations.

claim: Quantitative proteomics reveals that in HeLa cells intersectin 1 and -2 are present at ~20–30% the level of EPS15/R.
source: Quantitative proteomics reveals that in HeLa cells intersectin 1 and -2 are present at ~20–30% the level of EPS15/R (Hein et al., 2015; Itzhak et al., 2016).
evidence: This is information from cited references.

claim: The experiments presented here reveal that the pioneers localized to the perimeter of clathrin-coated structures at steady state are generally necessary for the inception of new clathrin-coated buds.
source: The experiments presented here reveal that the pioneers localized to the perimeter of clathrin-coated structures at steady state (Sochacki et al., 2017; Ma et al., 2016; Tebar et al., 1996; Henne et al., 2010; Edeling et al., 2006) are generally necessary for the inception of new clathrin-coated buds.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the data, supported by citations.

claim: The diminished number and/or intensity of AP-2 puncta in clone #40 cells highlights the supportive role the FCHO1/2-EPS15/R partnership plays in stabilizing active, conformationally-rearranged AP-2 at the cell surface.
source: Because HeLa clone #40 cells clearly have PtdIns(4,5)P2 in the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane when Akap1-Nb E_142-iRFP is expressed, the diminished number and/or intensity of AP-2 puncta in these cells highlights the supportive role the FCHO1/2-EPS15/R partnership plays in stabilizing active, conformationally-rearranged AP-2 at the cell surface.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in clone #40 cells.

claim: The still normal abundance of cytosolic AP-2 and clathrin in multiply genome-edited cells tends to argue strongly against AP-2 pairs simply engaging the PtdIns(4,5)P2-rich plasma membrane and simultaneously interacting with a clathrin triskelion to initiate stable, productive clathrin coat assembly.
source: The still normal abundance of cytosolic AP-2 and clathrin in these multiply genome-edited cells tends to argue strongly against AP-2 pairs simply engaging the PtdIns(4,5)P2-rich plasma membrane and simultaneously interacting with a clathrin triskelion to initiate stable, productive clathrin coat assembly (Cocucci et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data, supported by a citation.

claim: Super-resolution microscopy of the AP-2 and clathrin distribution at the ventral surface in single HeLa cells reveals substantial amounts of membrane-deposited AP-2 without a coincident clathrin signal.
source: Indeed, super-resolution microscopy of the AP-2 and clathrin distribution at the ventral surface in single HeLa cells reveals substantial amounts of membrane-deposited AP-2 without a coincident clathrin signal (Leyton-Puig et al., 2017).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: The intrinsically disordered linker in Fcho1/2 appears to act as a regulator of AP-2 switching from the closed to the open state.
source: While it is possible that a priming FCHO1/2•EPS15/R nanocluster (Ma et al., 2016) operates downstream or alongside AP-2 colliding with the plasma membrane in a suitable orientation to engage PtdIns(4,5)P2 through the binding sites on the large α- and β2-subunit trunks (Jackson et al., 2010; Gaidarov et al., 1996), the fact that the intrinsically disordered linker in Fcho1/2 appears to act as a regulator of AP-2 switching from the closed to the open state (Umasankar et al., 2014; Hollopeter et al., 2014) suggests that these pioneers promote the stable association of AP-2 with the membrane.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data, supported by citations.

claim: The strongest evidence for the model that pioneers promote the stable association of AP-2 with the membrane is the unmistakable reconstitution of apparently normal AP-2 puncta in the presence of a membrane-tethered FCHO1 linker domain in clone #40 cells.
source: The strongest evidence for this model is the unmistakable reconstitution of apparently normal AP-2 puncta in the presence of a membrane-tethered FCHO1 linker domain in clone #40 cells (Figure 11).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in clone #40 cells, with reference to Figure 11.

claim: Under normal circumstances at the edge of a de novo forming coat, membrane-attached FCHO1/2 interacts with incoming EPS15/R through the μHD, steering the AP-2-bound EPS15 to relay the heterotetramer to FCHO1/2 for local access to the activating linker.
source: Under normal circumstances at the edge of a de novo forming coat, membrane-attached FCHO1/2 interacts with incoming EPS15/R through the μHD (Ma et al., 2016; Shimada et al., 2016), steering the AP-2-bound EPS15 to relay the heterotetramer to FCHO1/2 for local access to the activating linker.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the data, supported by citations.

claim: This concept is in line with EPS15/R being the highest affinity binding partner of the FCHO1/2 μHD.
source: This concept is in line with EPS15/R being the highest affinity binding partner of the FCHO1/2 μHD (Umasankar et al., 2012; Shimada et al., 2016) and being the only proteins in the genome with the tandem DPFX2-3DPFX2-3DPF SLiMs necessary for optimal μHD engagement, both FCHO1/2 (Umasankar et al., 2012; Henne et al., 2007) and EPS15 (Wang et al., 2016b) binding to PtdIns(4,5)P2, and the interdomain linker of FCHO1/2 regulating AP-2 (Umasankar et al., 2014; Hollopeter et al., 2014) to rearrange the μ2 subunit to co-align PtdIns(4,5)P2, YXXØ and [DE]XXXL[LI] cargo binding interaction surfaces at the planar plasma membrane (Jackson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The data are also consistent with these rim-localized pioneers being able to drive deposition of new, open AP-2 into the interior of the incipient lattice.
source: The data are also consistent with these rim-localized pioneers being able to drive deposition of new, open AP-2 into the interior of the incipient lattice.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data.

claim: Large, long-lived clathrin assemblies in human embryonic stem cell-derived fibroblasts correlate with elevated expression levels of AP-2.
source: It has recently been demonstrated that large, long-lived clathrin assemblies in human embryonic stem cell-derived fibroblasts correlate with elevated expression levels of AP-2 (Dambournet et al., 2018).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: Even with high soluble levels of AP-2 and PtdIns(4,5)P2, normally sized and distributed clathrin-coated structures on the plasma membrane require the activity of EPS15/R and FCHO1/2.
source: Strikingly, while this may be mechanistically related to the abnormal clathrin-coated structures in the genome-edited HeLa clone #64/1.E and clone #40 cells, due to an increase in the cytosolic AP-2 pool, the effect of EPS15 impoundment in clone #40 cells shown here indicates that even with high soluble levels of AP-2 and PtdIns(4,5)P2, normally sized and distributed clathrin-coated structures on the plasma membrane require the activity of EPS15/R and FCHO1/2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in clone #40 cells.

claim: Conditionally hematopoietic compartment compound-null Eps15-/-/Eps15L1-/- mice are anemic due to dysfunctional erythrocyte differentiation and maturation.
source: It has also just been reported that conditionally hematopoietic compartment compound-null Eps15-/-/Eps15L1-/- mice are anemic due to dysfunctional erythrocyte differentiation and maturation (Milesi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference.

claim: The Eps15-/-/Eps15L1-/- double knock-out mice display strikingly abnormal accumulation of the transferrin receptor on the surface of the defective circulating red blood cell population.
source: Remarkably, although the transferrin receptor is the prototypical AP-2-dependent YXXØ-signal-harboring transmembrane receptor (Traub and Bonifacino, 2013; Collawn et al., 1990), the Eps15-/-/Eps15L1-/- double knock-out mice display strikingly abnormal accumulation of the transferrin receptor on the surface of the defective circulating red blood cell population (Milesi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is information from a cited reference, supported by citations.

claim: The dysregulation of the efficient internalization of the transferrin receptor in the erythrocyte precursor cells (reticulocytes) expressing normal AP-2 is reminiscent of the phenotype of HeLa clone #40 cells with Nb E_142-mediated sequestration of EPS15.
source: This dysregulation of the efficient internalization of the transferrin receptor in the erythrocyte precursor cells (reticulocytes) expressing normal AP-2 is obviously reminiscent of the phenotype of HeLa clone #40 cells with Nb E_142-mediated sequestration of EPS15 shown here, and independently reiterates the upstream role of Eps15/R (and Fcho1/2) in the proper functioning of the AP-2 adaptor complex under normal conditions.
evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings to the mouse model data, supported by a citation.
